parsed.reason: Checked each state against the spec. WL/WR: a low ground goes to FALLL/FALLR, which takes precedence over dig (to DIGL/DIGR), which takes precedence over bump (WL<->WR swap, so bump_left turns a walker right and bump_right turns it left). Both bumps together still switch direction. DIGL/DIGR stay digging while ground=1 and go to FALLL/FALLR when ground=0, matching the 'dig until the other side' behavior. FALLL/FALLR ignore bumps and dig, and on ground=1 return to the same walking direction. DEAD is absorbing, and all outputs are 0 in DEAD. The fall counter resets outside fall states, increments during fall, and saturates at 20. Tracing the timing: the counter is 0 in the first aaah cycle and equals N when ground returns on the cycle after N falling cycles. So DEAD is entered when N>=20, which means aaah was high for at least 21 cycles including the landing cycle. That matches 'falls for more than 20 clock cycles'. Under the other reading (count only the ground-low cycles) the threshold would be off by one, so the threshold is the only real ambiguity. The next-state logic assigns `next` in every case branch, so there are no latches. Outputs are decoded from the state register, so the machine is Moore. Async reset goes to WL. Overall the RTL matches the spec under the most natural interpretation.
